reasons: § 2.2's sole-and-exclusive sourcing obligation is a customer-side commitment of 100% of analytics demand with no reduction, notice or true-up mechanic, so it fails the MINCOMMIT fallback (12-month limit, 30-day reduction, true-up) even though §§ 2.1, 7.1 and 12.3 are favourable — the deviation classification is correct and not an upgrade of an already-acceptable fallback.

The redline is directionally right and actionable: it converts Vendor to a non-exclusive provider and confirms payment only for Services ordered, which reaches the preferred position (no minimum/volume restriction) and also resolves the direct conflict with § 12.3.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.747 changed-character ratio) is explained by the clause being a single short sentence whose exclusivity obligation must be replaced wholesale; no smaller edit removes the exclusivity. The appended 'no minimum volume / pay only for Services ordered' language duplicates § 2.1 and could be trimmed, but it is harmless and does not create new obligations on Customer.
Comment is accurate (correctly describes the deletion, cites the playbook position and the § 12.3 contradiction), concise, first-person plural, and properly prefixed.
